message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for North Carolina Avenue.

I have $726 and a pink monopoly. The opponent has dark blue and is building heavily on Boardwalk and Park Place.

p4 currently leads at $85. I will bid up to about $150 and drop out. This wins the auction at or below mortgage value, nets cash after mortgaging, and prevents p4 from completing a PA+NC pair.

p4 cannot complete a green monopoly even with North Carolina, since Pacific Avenue is mortgaged by p1. p1 has only $29 cash and a dangerous dark blue monopoly. Hotels remain available.

All 32 houses are currently in play, so no one can build more until someone sells. If I buy North Carolina for $86 and mortgage it immediately, I would recover $150 and end up with $640 cash.

Blocking p4 from a second green is not a major concern, since they already own mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue and would still need Pacific from the nearly broke p1. The real danger is p1's dark blue monopoly: Park Place with three houses charges $1100 in rent, and Boardwalk with four houses charges $1700. Those heavy rent payments are the priority.

I can sell all twelve pink houses to raise $600. Combined with my $726 cash, I have $1326 in total liquidity. That covers the $1100 rent on Park Place and the $1700 rent on Boardwalk.

The $1326 liquidity covers Park Place but not Boardwalk. Boardwalk requires mortgaging properties with houses still on them, which is impossible without selling first. The current bid of $85 is still well below the $150 cap.

I will not jump bid. I will continue raising by one dollar each turn to force p4 to bleed cash until they exceed the $150 cap.

I should confirm whether mortgaging happens automatically or requires a separate action. I also need to consider what happens if p1 goes bankrupt, since their assets would be auctioned or returned to creditors.

Standard Monopoly rent for four houses on the pink properties is $625 on St. Charles Place, $625 on States Avenue, and $900 on Virginia Avenue. p1 has only $29 cash.

If p1 lands on my pink properties, they would go bankrupt to me and I would inherit their dark blue monopoly. This makes keeping my houses critical. I should only sell houses if I cannot cover a rent payment.

p4 is in jail with $763 and owns a light blue monopoly with four houses each. Oriental charges $400 in rent with four houses. Vermont charges $400. Connecticut charges $450.

I will bid $86. p4 has matched every previous bid, so they likely continue. I may win at $150 or drop if they exceed it.

Forcing p4 to pay over $150 is especially harmful because North Carolina is not a true monopoly for them. They cannot build houses without Pacific Avenue, so the property is mainly a blocker or trade chip. Paying more than the $150 mortgage value locks cash into an asset that can only be recovered by mortgaging it again and paying 10% interest to unmortgage later.

Dropping at $85 would give p4 the property cheaply. The $150 cap is a denial-for-free strategy: buying for $150 and mortgaging returns exactly $150, so I break even but deny them the property. Anything above $150 costs me cash relative to mortgaging. I also need to weigh the strategic value of owning a mortgaged North Carolina, since unmortgaging it later would cost $165.

Denying p4 North Carolina is strategically valuable. If they won it cheaply, they could trade with the nearly broke p1 to complete a green monopoly. That would give them a dangerous three-way split against my pink monopoly. Keeping the property out of their hands prevents that deal.

Owning North Carolina even mortgaged permanently blocks any green monopoly. Neither p1 nor p4 can complete greens without it, so the property remains a strategic anchor regardless of whether it is mortgaged or not.

The blocking value of North Carolina likely exceeds its $150 mortgage value, so the bid cap should be higher than $150. With no houses remaining on the greens, no player can build there yet. The blocking value is purely strategic.

p1 cannot hotel Boardwalk because it costs $200 and they only have $29. p4 could hotel all three light blues for $150 and free twelve houses, but that would not help them build greens since they do not own a buildable monopoly beyond light blues.

Hoteling the light blue properties would return twelve houses to the bank, allowing p1 to build more on dark blues if they acquire cash. The green monopoly threat is medium-term because no houses remain on the greens yet. I must keep enough liquidity to cover the $1100 rent on Park Place and the $1700 rent on Boardwalk.

Selling all twelve pink houses and mortgaging three properties yields $1546 total liquidity. That is still $154 short of the $1700 rent on Boardwalk with four houses. I cannot survive that payment and would go bankrupt to p1 if I land there.

Winning North Carolina under $150 would raise my cash after mortgaging. I should try to win the auction at a low price rather than just drive the bid up. If p4 keeps matching, I may not reach that low price and dropping out is the safer choice.

I cannot know p4's true cap. They might bid well above $150 because they already own Pennsylvania Avenue. I will hold at $150 and drop if they exceed it.

I will not jump to $150 now. That would end the auction and force p4 to bid $151 or drop, but if their cap is below $150 they would have dropped earlier anyway. I will keep bidding $86 and only mortgage immediately if I win under $150.
